subject: SLA exception framework & trial discount request — Redwood inference
messages:
From: Elliot Gardner <elliot.gardner@nimbus.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood trial — SLA ask and one-off concession?

Hi Naomi,

We kicked off an internal review after the demo. Legal and Ops are broadly happy, but two items are blocking our pilot approval:

1) Uptime guarantee during the 90-day pilot — our security team wants explicit uptime tiers and a short crediting mechanism if we see persistent issues.
2) A temporary escalation SLT (named contact + 30‑minute response during business hours) for the first 30 days of the trial while we run integration smoke tests.

Nimbus is a mid-market customer but this pilot could scale quickly across our platform. We were wondering if Redwood can offer a one-time trial concession:
- A pilot-specific uptime commitment 99.5% for core inference across two regions
- A trial credit pool (pro-rated) if uptime drops below the band
- A dedicated escalation contact for the first 30 days (not a full enterprise retainer)

Can you share how flexible you can be on a short-term SLA exception and what pricing/credits that would entail? Procurement would like an official term sheet for internal sign-off.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Gardner
Director, Platform Integrations
Nimbus Systems

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Gardner <elliot.gardner@nimbus.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial — SLA ask and one-off concession?

Hi Elliot — appreciated the clear ask and congrats on the smooth demo.

Short answer: we can support a pilot-specific SLA exception with a temporary escalation contact and a small pool of uptime credits. To keep things simple for Procurement, I attached a term sheet draft and a proposed SLA summary. High level proposal:

- Pilot SLA: 99.5% availability for inference in the two specified regions for the 90-day pilot window.
- Credit structure: pro-rated token-credit pool equal to 5% of estimated billable tokens for the pilot if we breach the 99.5% band for more than one rolling 7-day period. Credits issue automatically to Nimbus billing account.
- Escalation cover: named escalation contact (Level 2 engineer) during business hours weekdays for the first 30 days, plus a once-daily check-in for the integration week.
- Pricing impact: one-time pilot concession = 10% off listed trial pricing OR equivalent credits applied (your choice).

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_v1.pdf (term summary), SLA_TermSheet_Nimbus.xlsx (credit calc + pricing).

If that looks directionally right, Ben and I can run internal approvals and flip a cleaned term sheet back to Procurement. Can you confirm the two regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1) and a target pilot start date?

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Gardner <elliot.gardner@nimbus.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial — SLA ask and one-off concession?

Thanks Naomi — that’s helpful and close to what we expected. A couple of clarifications from Procurement and Security:

- The credit trigger looks good, but Procurement prefers a stepped credit schedule rather than a single pool (so we can map to observed downtime severity). Something like:
  * 99.0–99.5%: 3% credit
  * 98.0–99.0%: 10% credit
  * <98.0%: 25% credit + optional pilot termination right

- For the escalation contact, can we have the named engineer’s escalation SLT in writing (title, escalate-to contact, and guaranteed weekdays 09:00–17:00 response SLA)? We don’t need 24/7 during the pilot but want clarity on accountability.

- Lastly, Procurement asks that the one-time concession be a credits-first approach (apply credits before discount) so accounting can show the concession as a service credit rather than a price markdown.

If you can adapt the term sheet to the stepped-credit schedule and provide the named escalation lead, we can move to internal sign-off and schedule the kickoff for 14 Apr.

—Elliot

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial — SLA ask and one-off concession?

Team — recapping Elliot’s counter and my suggested internal approach for approvals:

1) Stepped credit schedule: acceptable as a pilot concession. Operationally we can map availability windows to credit issuance; finance prefers credits-first (so accounting works out).

2) Named escalation lead: I can assign Maria Lopes (Senior L2 SRE) as the contact for the 30-day escalation window. She’s available weekdays 09:00–17:00 PT and will respond within 30 minutes to acknowledged incidents. Contact: maria.lopes@redwood.ai. We’ll include her title and escalation path in the term sheet.

3) Pricing mechanics: Instead of a 10% upfront discount, propose the credits-first model and offer an additional one-time 5% purchase credit if the pilot converts to a committed Dedicated contract within 90 days of pilot close. That keeps list pricing intact and gives Nimbus a tangible conversion incentive.

4) Legal redlines: Jonas — can you sign off quickly on termination right for <98% availability during a 7-day rolling window? We should limit customer termination to pilot-only and require a remediation period (48 hours to investigate) before escalation to termination rights.

If legal is good, Naomi please send a revised term sheet back to Elliot today so procurement can start paperwork.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Gardner <elliot.gardner@nimbus.com>, Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, maria.lopes <maria.lopes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial — SLA ask and one-off concession?

Elliot — appreciate the quick review and helpful specifics. Attached is a revised term sheet that:

- Replaces the single credit pool with the stepped schedule you requested (99.0–99.5% / 98.0–99.0% / <98.0%).
- Lists Maria Lopes as the named escalation lead for weekdays 09:00–17:00 PT with a 30-minute acknowledged response SLA.
- Specifies the pilot-only termination right if availability falls below 98% after a documented remediation window (48 hours) and gives Redwood the opportunity to remediate before termination.
- Implements credits-first mechanics; any additional conversion incentive is captured as a one-time 5% purchase credit if Nimbus signs a Dedicated contract within 90 days after pilot completion.

Next steps: if Procurement is happy, sign off and we’ll issue a DocuSign link for the pilot term sheet. Proposed start date stands at 2026-04-14. If that timing doesn’t work, let me know and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_SLA_v1.pdf (term summary), SLA_TermSheet_Nimbus.xlsx (detailed credit calc)
